content.value_statement: Generic interfaces weaken product trust and make AI output easy to spot. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward distinctive frontend design.
actual_capabilities: Provides guidance for typography, color, spacing, motion, interaction, responsive layout, and UX writing.
Points agents to reference files for detailed design rules and implementation checks.
Encourages production-grade code with functional interfaces, accessible states, and responsive behavior.
Defines visual anti-patterns to avoid common AI-generated layouts, colors, cards, and typography.
Includes CSS examples for focus rings, motion, grid layout, safe areas, and font loading.
limitations: It does not include runnable source code, tests, or packaged components.
It cannot verify final visual quality without a browser review or screenshot inspection.
It may conflict with strict brand systems that require conservative typography and layouts.
It offers design guidance, not legal compliance or full accessibility certification.

use_cases.title: Design a memorable product page
use_cases.description: Use the skill to turn a product brief into a distinctive page with clear typography, spacing, motion, and responsive behavior.

use_cases.title: Upgrade a working interface
use_cases.description: Apply the guidance to refine an existing component with stronger hierarchy, better states, and more polished interactions.

use_cases.title: Prototype a startup UI
use_cases.description: Move from a vague app idea to a focused interface direction that avoids generic AI patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Design a component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a focused UI element.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a distinctive frontend component for [purpose]. Use the frontend-design skill to choose typography, spacing, color, states, and responsive behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Build a responsive page
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a complete screen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a responsive [page type] for [audience]. Use the skill guidance for visual direction, layout rhythm, accessibility, motion, and UX writing.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an existing interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this interface and improve it with the frontend-design skill. Focus on hierarchy, typography, color contrast, interaction states, and mobile adaptation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a complete UI system
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a connected design direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a cohesive UI direction for [product]. Define visual principles, reusable patterns, responsive rules, motion behavior, and implementation details for production use.

output_examples.input: A task management dashboard for a small design studio.
output_examples.output: A polished dashboard concept with strong hierarchy, clear task states, responsive navigation, accessible focus treatment, and restrained motion.

output_examples.input: A pricing page that currently looks like a generic card grid.
output_examples.output: A revised pricing experience with clearer plan comparison, distinctive typography, fewer repeated cards, stronger calls to action, and mobile-specific layout choices.

output_examples.input: A form flow for onboarding new team members.
output_examples.output: An onboarding flow with visible labels, helpful error copy, clear progress states, large touch targets, and thoughtful empty states.

best_practices: Give product context, audience, tone, and technical constraints before asking for implementation.
Ask for responsive, accessible states and screenshot review when visual quality matters.
Use the reference guidance as a starting point, then align choices with your brand system.
anti_patterns: Requesting a generic modern layout without audience, tone, or visual direction.
Applying every visual effect at once instead of choosing a clear design concept.
Ignoring accessibility, motion reduction, and mobile behavior during final review.

faq.question: Does this skill generate code?
faq.answer: It guides an AI assistant to implement frontend code, but the skill package itself contains design guidance files.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it only for landing pages?
faq.answer: No. It can guide components, application screens, artifacts, posters, and complete frontend experiences.

faq.question: Can it follow an existing brand system?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the brand rules first so the assistant adapts the guidance to your constraints.

faq.question: Does it replace accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No. It includes accessibility guidance, but final work still needs testing with real tools and users.

faq.question: Why does it include many design rules?
faq.answer: The rules help agents avoid generic patterns and make clearer choices about typography, color, layout, motion, and writing.
